title: Habitats and Survival
seo_title: Grade 3 Habitats Worksheets: Which Living Things Survive in Each Habitat
standard_text: Construct an argument with evidence that in a particular habitat some organisms can survive well, some survive less well, and some cannot survive at all.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on habitats and survival (NGSS 3-LS4-3): deserts, the Arctic, oceans, ponds, rain forests and grasslands, traits that fit a habitat, and plant survival data. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Living things survive best in habitats that fit their traits.
key_sub: In each habitat some living things survive well, some less well and some not at all.
body_html:
How to think about it

A habitat is the place where a living thing gets food, water, shelter and space. Deserts, the Arctic, oceans, ponds, rain forests, grasslands and forests are habitats.

In a habitat, some living things survive well, some survive less well and some cannot survive at all. Their traits must fit the habitat: a camel can go a long time without water, a polar bear has thick fur and fat, a fish has gills.

Example

Could a polar bear survive in a hot desert?

It has thick fur and fat for the cold.

Answer: No, it would get too hot.

Example

Where would a cactus survive best?

A cactus stores water.

Answer: in a desert

Common mistakes

  • Thinking any animal can live anywhere if it tries.
  • Forgetting that plants need the right habitat too.
  • Thinking a living thing changes its body right away when moved.

faq.a: A habitat is the place where a living thing gets the food, water, shelter and space it needs.

faq.q: Why can't every animal live in every habitat?
faq.a: Its traits fit some places better than others. A fish needs water to breathe, and a polar bear needs cold.

faq.q: What happens when a habitat changes?
faq.a: Some living things may survive less well or have to move, and others may start to survive better.
